title: Why You Shouldn't Forget This Powerful Back-To-School Strategy
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Michael Linsin argues that while establishing routines, procedures, and classroom leadership presence is essential at the start of the school year, the real number-one goal for the first few days should be getting students to genuinely love being in the class. He dispels the misconception that this requires elaborate, high-preparation activities, instead identifying humor as a low-effort, high-impact way to build rapport quickly. Linsin reassures teachers that special comedic talent isn't required — sharing embarrassing stories, self-deprecating humor, and simply being willing to laugh with students is enough, since 'school is a target-rich environment and kids are inherently funny.' He explains that humor makes high expectations feel more palatable and eases the stress of the early school year for students. The piece frames humor as a shortcut to building the kind of influential relationship that makes every other management strategy work better.
points: Building routines, rules, and leadership presence is essential at the start of the year, but the primary goal should be getting students to love being in the class.
This does not require elaborate or high-preparation activities — humor is a low-effort, high-impact way to build rapport quickly.
No special comedic talent is needed; self-deprecating stories and a willingness to laugh with students are enough, since kids are naturally drawn to humor.
Humor makes high, potentially shocking expectations feel more palatable and eases students' stress during a naturally tense time of year.
Humor is described as one of the fastest ways to build an influential relationship with a new class, which in turn makes behavior, motivation, and achievement easier.
quotes: But you also can’t forget one of the most powerful strategies of all.
You see, for all that stuff to work as it should, to get your students to care enough to listen, to motivate them, intrinsically, to want to buy-in, they have to enjoy being there.
So my number one goal those first few days of school isn’t just to lay the groundwork. It’s to get them to love being in my class.
Now, it’s important to point out that you don’t need any special talent or ability to use humor in your classroom.
Humor is everywhere. School is a target-rich environment and kids are inherently funny. They love to laugh and appreciate any attempt to make them smile.
It makes your sky-high standards and expectations, which can be a shock to the system, more palatable. It puts your students at ease during what can be a stressful time for them.
